nodes.label: Lead pipeline feed for kanban and list views
Lead search across raw name, email and phone columns
Lead score bands (hot / warm / cold / risk)
Lead to blacklist-match linkage on the lead row
Lead conversion trail to a rental (converted_at / converted_to_rental_id)
Per-tenant lockbox message templates (email / SMS / WhatsApp)
Built-in default lockbox templates used when a tenant has saved none
{{variable}} placeholder contract shared with the notification senders
One template row per channel, upserted by channel lookup rather than a DB unique key
Maintenance banner surfacing (platform-global plus per-tenant)
Rationale: a tenant's own banner takes priority over the platform-global one
Banner polled every 60s so a platform incident notice reaches open tabs
Client-side RBAC gating for managers and read-only roles
READ_ONLY_ROLES — roles whose entire definition is may-look-may-not-change
Rationale: ops is deliberately NOT read-only — it is a working role gated by canEdit across the portal
canEdit — the single write gate every mutation control in the portal renders behind
Rationale: canEdit used to open with `if (!isManager) return true`, handing write access to viewers
Rationale: this is UX gating only — the real gate lives in each edge function's auth block
Rationale: a super admin never reaches the role checks — the auth store rewrites their role to head_admin
Nested settings sub-tab gating (parent `settings` grant required first)
Route exceptions: dashboard and /subscription always open, /users always closed to managers
Lead-to-vehicle matching engine invocation
Match option kinds — single, stitched (multi-vehicle) and conditional offers
Match results cached by leadId + last_activity_at so edits re-run the engine
Operator prompt to migrate onto their own Stripe account (off / soft / hard)
Rationale: both migration tasks are DERIVED, never stored, so a satisfied operator is never stuck on a hard block
Rationale: OAuth always links the LIVE account regardless of stripe_mode — connecting is a one-time business action
?oauth= return toast handling, deduped against own-stripe-settings via returnTo scoping
Rationale: pending flags are latched, not reset — the button must spin until the browser leaves
Rationale: tenantId is always sent because a super admin's app_users.tenant_id is NULL
Rationale: migration columns are absent from TenantContext (~40 admin fields) so they need their own scoped query
Read-only twin of useMigrationBlocker for the setup-reminder interlock
Success-linger interlock mirroring SUCCESS_LINGER_MS so the reminder never flashes under the celebration
Rationale: MIGRATION_COLUMNS must stay byte-identical in both hooks — they share one React Query row
hideStripeTask — the migration flow owns the Connect-Stripe step while a tenant is mid-migration
Rationale: the twin omits the ?oauth= side effect because mounting the full blocker twice fires the toast twice
768px mobile breakpoint detection for responsive portal chrome
Staff notification inbox (read, mark-read, delete, clear)
user_id NULL means a tenant-wide broadcast every staff member sees
Realtime channel subscribes to the whole notifications table and filters tenant/user in JS
Organisation settings read/write through the `settings` edge function
_tenant_id smuggled into the update body for multi-tenant audit logging
Hardcoded legacy 'Drive 917' branding used as placeholder data when the settings fetch fails
org-settings query key carries no tenant id, breaking the repo-wide cache-isolation convention
Operator payment-mode switches (payment_mode automated/manual, booking_payment_mode manual/auto)
Reminder preference toggles (due today, overdue 1d, overdue multi, due soon 2d)
Vehicle-owner payout lifecycle — create, record payment, cancel
Manual net-owed safety valve that bypasses commission math entirely
Rationale: per-vehicle double-payout protection lives inside calculate_owner_owed, so an empty preview means nothing left to pay
Client-side rollback deletes the payout header when the line insert fails (no DB transaction)
Payout status transitions pending → partially_paid → paid, decided client-side from amount_paid vs net_owed
Negative net_owed is refused — the operator must carry it forward to the next payout
Per-owner realised revenue reporting over a date range
Owner-owed preview computed server-side so commission math is not duplicated in the client
Assigning / unassigning a vehicle to a fleet owner
Per-vehicle commission overrides (type, value, flat-fee period) layered over the owner default
Commission overrides are cleared when a vehicle is unassigned so they cannot leak to the next owner
Pay-as-you-go rolling daily invoice statement for a rental
Rationale: the ledger is the money truth — balance due comes from ledger_entries.remaining_amount, not the accrual rolling total
Cumulative per-category totals reset the moment an invoice reaches status 'paid'
UI mirrors every gate inside send-payg-reminders so it can explain why reminders are not sending
Rationale: polling restored to 30s/60s production cadence after the 5-minute test day, cutting query load ~12x
Realtime subscription on the four PAYG tables with polling kept as a websocket-drop backstop
Daily rate falls back to computePaygDailyRate — same formula as the cron — before the first accrual lands
Reminder cadence resolution: per-rental override → tenant default → built-in 4 days
pg-NNN invoice reference derived client-side from accrual_day_index (no stored invoice number)
PAYG accrual ledger totals (rental, tax, service fee, outstanding)
Rationale: 15s staleTime because the accrual cron writes every 15 minutes
Chronological PAYG timeline — accruals, payments, refunds, reminders and projections
Reminder countdown mirrors the cron: grace_days from payg_start_ts first, then interval_days from last sent
Charge-to-day-index mapping via payg_accruals.ledger_entry_ids, so a payment can be attributed to specific days
payment_applications is fetched tenant-wide (no rental filter) and joined in memory
Reminder cap surfaced as a synthetic timeline event so the UI can warn at the limit
Refund events are derived from the same payments row (refund_amount / refund_status), not a separate table
Payment link / request history across rental, customer and tenant-wide views
derivePaymentLinks — one status derivation shared by all three payment-link surfaces
Rationale: precedence deposit-hold > paid > voided > staff decision > superseded > expired > awaiting, so money-in-hand always wins
Rationale: targetKey includes customer_id and amount so two customers' account-level links never collapse into a false 'superseded'
Rationale: checkout.session.expired only cancels the rental and never flips the payments row, so age is the only 'expired' signal
Rationale: an uncaptured pre-auth can carry status Applied/Partial — authorized is not money in hand
Rationale: reject_payment only flips verification_status, so without an explicit branch a declined payment shows as an open link
Extension links are the only ones with a stored reusable customer URL, joined from rental_extensions
Tenant-wide Payment Requests view on the Invoices page, enriched with customer name
Staff approve/reject flow for manually recorded payments
Approve then allocate: approve_payment RPC followed by the apply-payment edge function
Rationale: an allocation failure is swallowed — the payment is approved and allocation can be retried
Rejecting a payment closes the rental and can release the vehicle (vehicle_released in the RPC result)
Customer rejection notification fired after reject, failure-tolerant
Fan-out invalidation of ~17 money query keys after each verification decision
Pending-payments badge count polled every 30s
Payments page data — filter, sort and server-paginate the payments table
Payments CSV export
Rationale: tenantId was optional and unset at the call site, so the export returned every tenant's payments — now required
Rationale: Status and 'Counts As Received' are load-bearing — a void keeps its full amount and would overstate revenue
Date filters hardcoded to America/New_York regardless of the tenant's own timezone setting
Vehicle search pre-queries the whole fleet and filters in JS before an `in` clause
Website bookings awaiting staff capture approval
The approval queue is defined purely as payments with booking_source='website' and capture_status='requires_capture'
Transient fetch errors are swallowed and the badge falls back to 0 rather than erroring
